description:
Sheet layout: a single landscape LADOT B-Permit signing and striping plan sheet at 1 inch = 40 feet, with a text area across the top (construction notes, legend, notes), a sign panel down the right edge, the plan view across the middle, and the consultant and LADOT title blocks along the bottom.

Construction notes block (top left and top center): eight numbered notes in three columns. Notes 1 and 2 (with sub-items A to C) cover responsibility for removal, markout and thermoplastic striping and the LADOT Citywide Investigations Unit inspection sequence. Notes 3 to 5 cover temporary raised pavement markers, changing field conditions with a two-year expiration, and parking meter removal and reinstallation. Notes 6, 7 and 8 are keyed to boxed numbers 6 and 7 on the plan and to the bike lane surface condition.

Legend (top right): item 1 shows three line pairs, a double solid line with an outline arrow for existing striping and markings to remain, a dashed pair with a dashed arrow for existing striping and markings to be removed, and a heavy double line with a solid arrow for proposed striping and markings. Item 2 shows three sign-and-post symbols for existing, existing to be removed or relocated, and proposed (with a filled dot). Item 3 shows a circled S for a signalized intersection. Item 4 shows R/C curb markings as a thin box (existing to remain), a dotted box (existing to be removed) and a heavy filled bar (proposed).

Notes block (below the legend): four short notes giving length of design, pavement markings, paint removal and the continental crosswalk standard drawing.

Sign panel (far right): a two-column grid of sign thumbnails with codes beneath each. Row 1: R3-4 (prohibition circle over a U-turn arrow) and R3-2 (prohibition circle over a turn arrow). Row 2: R9-3 (prohibition circle over a pedestrian) and R9-3bP(RT) (USE CROSSWALK with a right arrow). Row 3: R9-3bP(LT) (left arrow USE CROSSWALK) and R61-7(CA) (lane-use sign with a through-and-left arrow and a right-turn arrow marked ONLY). Row 4: R3-7(RT) (RIGHT LANE MUST TURN RIGHT) and SW44(LT)(CA) (diamond with a diagonal arrow pointing down and to the left). Row 5: ASSEMBLY A (school pedestrian pentagon with a SCHOOL plaque) and R61-19(CA) (two curved arrows, left and right, each marked ONLY). The remaining cells in the panel are blank.

Plan view: A Avenue runs left to right through two signalized intersections, B Street at the left and C Street at the right, and the plan shows the avenue from west of B Street to east of C Street. Both side streets are signalized (circled S). Land uses are labeled around the blocks: Theater and Mini Mall at the northwest, McDonalds Restaurant, Commercial and Industrial along the north side, Orchard Supply Hardware at the southwest, Proposed Development at the south-center, Post Office, Restaurant and Commercial along the south side east of C Street.

West of B Street: the roadway is dimensioned 10 ft (north parking lane), 30 ft, 30 ft and 20 ft (south side), 90 ft overall. The centerline is a double solid line and the two travel directions each have lane lines and 8 inch white (8"W.) striping. Lane-shift tapers are labeled 190 ft taper at 27:1 and 150 ft taper at 50:1, with JOIN callouts where new striping meets existing, offset labels of 10 ft and 20 ft, and cross-section offsets of 18 ft and 17 ft. Faint pavement legends XING and PED are shown near the intersection. Parking time limits and tow-away text are given on both sides: T.A.N.S.A.T. 4-7 PM X-Sat & Sun, PMZ 1 Hour Parking 9am to 4pm Mon-Fri, 8am to 8pm Sat. Sign R2-1(35) is on the north curb. Crossed boxes mark curb areas along both curbs. Corner radius CR=25 ft is noted at the northwest corner.

B Street intersection: continental (ladder-bar) crosswalks are drawn on all four legs, with callouts WHITE and boxed 6 for note 6. Sign callouts R3-4, R10-7, R41(CA) and R3-2 are placed at the corners. Bus zones are marked at the northwest and northeast corners. The north leg of B Street is dimensioned 17 ft, 35 ft, 40 ft and 10 ft, 102 ft overall, with lane widths of 10.5 ft, 10 ft, 10 ft, 9 ft (center left-turn or median lane), 10 ft, 10 ft and 15.5 ft and a 264 ft 8"W. line. The south leg is dimensioned 15 ft, 35 ft, 40 ft and 15 ft, 105 ft overall, with the same lane widths, a 130 ft R/C length, a 170 ft 8"W. line and a left-turn arrow. Sign callouts at the south side include R3-7(RT), 171 ft R/C and R3-4. Right-turn and left-turn arrows are drawn in the A Avenue lanes at the intersection. On the A Avenue roadway at B Street the dimensions 40 ft and 35 ft are stacked, with lane widths of 12 ft, 10 ft, 10 ft, 10 ft and 12 ft, and 95 ft 8"W. lines on both sides of the center.

A Avenue between B and C Streets: proposed 110 ft 8"W. and 210 ft 8"W. edge and lane lines, 5 ft (TYP.) and 20 ft (TYP.) spacing at the B Street crosswalk, a 12 inch yellow line (12" YELLOW) forming an S-curve over a 60 ft length near the center, and an 80 ft 8"W. line toward C Street. Proposed R/C lengths are 110 ft (south side near B Street), 100 ft R/C (south side near C Street) and 30 ft R/C (north side near C Street). Dimensions at the right of the middle block read 40 ft, 102 ft and 37 ft with 25 ft, 22 ft, 15 ft and 13 ft. Sign callouts include R3-7(RT), REMOVE W11-2, REMOVE R9-3a(2) and R9-3b(2), and (2)R9-3a with (2)R9-3b(RT/LT). Property lines are shown as Existing PL and PROPOSED PL with a 2 ft DEDICATION. Parking text on the south side reads A.G.Z. T.A.N.S. 7-9AM, 4-7PM X-SAT & SUN., PMZ 1 HOUR PARKING 9AM-4PM MON-FRI, 8AM-8PM SAT. and REINSTALL T.A.N.S.A.T. On the north side the text reads T.A.N.S.A.T. 4pm-7pm X-Sat & Sun, N.P.A.T. A red rectangle drawn around the lower-center part of the plan (the south curb area from the 2 ft dedication to the C Street crosswalk) is a review markup overlay on the sheet and is not part of the standard drawing.

C Street intersection: continental crosswalks on all four legs with WHITE and boxed 6 callouts. Signs REMOVE R1-5a and REMOVE R1-5, R5-2(6 Tons), SW44(LT)(CA), R61-19(CA) (shown twice along the east curb) and REMOVE (2)W11-2 with (2)W16-7p are called out. The south leg of C Street is dimensioned 10 ft, 20 ft, 20 ft and 10 ft, 60 ft overall, with a 60 ft taper at 30:1, lane widths of 18 ft, 10 ft and 12 ft, a 100 ft 8"W. line, 68 ft R/C and 40 ft R/C lengths, left-turn and right-turn arrows, and 5 ft (TYP.) at the crosswalk. Corner radii are CR=25 ft and CR=10 ft at the south corners and CR=15 ft at the northeast. Text beside the south leg reads RE-INSTALL 30 Min. Parking 8am to 6pm X-Sun. East of C Street the avenue is dimensioned 10 ft, 30 ft, 30 ft and 10 ft, 80 ft overall, with a 120 ft 8"W. line, a 60 ft S-curve transition with JOIN callouts, lane widths of 10 ft, 12 ft and 18 ft, R/C lengths and signs R3-2 and REMOVE W11-2. Parking text on the south side reads A.G.Z. T.A.N.S. 1-9am, 4-7pm X-Sat & Sun PMZ 1 Hour Parking 9am to 4pm Mon-Fri, 8am to 8pm Sat. T.A.N.S.A.T. N.P.A.T. is shown along the north side.

Scales and orientation: a north arrow in a circle and the text Scale: 1" = 40' are at the lower center right. A bar scale along the bottom is labeled 1"=20' ORIGINAL MAP SCALE 1"=40', with the upper scale from 20 to 100 FEET and the lower scale from 40 to 200 FEET.

Title blocks: at the lower left is the professional certification block with the statement that the plan is prepared by and under the responsible charge of the named consulting firm and California Registered Engineers shown below, a PRIVATE CONSULTANT LOGO/ADDRESS box, two circular Registered Professional Engineer seals for the State of California, No. XXXXX Civil and No. XXXXX Traffic, and the City of Los Angeles Business Tax Registration No. ########-##. The marking (LADOT Revised 4/19) (Drafting Std. 11/04) is below. At the lower right is the LADOT block with Reviewed and Accepted signature lines for Transportation Engineer and Senior Transportation Engineer, the INSTALLATION DATES box (Markout began, Markout completed, Striping completed), District XXXX, References XXXX, the CITY OF LOS ANGELES DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION name with Seleta J. Reynolds, General Manager, the sheet title "A" AVENUE BET "B" STREET AND "C" STREET, a two-year implementation warning, Project No. B-PERMIT#, Drawing No. A-XXXX, sheet 1 of X, and SHEET OF and INDEX NUMBER boxes. A vertical revision strip at the far right has columns for No., Revision Description, T.E., Date, By, District, Bikeways, T.E.A., T.E., S.T.E., Date and Reviewed.
notes:
Construction notes:
1. The B-Permittee shall be responsible for labor and material involved in the removal, markout, and installation of all striping, pavement markings, and signs shown hereon. Removal of markings shall be performed before markout and installation of new striping, and shall be by wet sandblasting/grinding in accordance with LADOT Specification No. 76-016-10. Markout shall be by heavy paint brush or spray paint over a pulled rope in the respective white or yellow colors of the proposed striping. Final striping and pavement markings shall be in hot applied alkyd thermoplastic in accordance with LADOT Specifications Nos. 51-005-10 and 76-012-15.
2. The installation of thermoplastic striping may proceed only after inspection and approval of markout by the LADOT Citywide Investigations Unit. The contractor shall correct all errors in markout requested by LADOT. Upon approval of markout the contractor shall fully install the thermoplastic striping, pavement markings (curb markings, and signs as applicable) within the following three (3) working days. The contractor shall contact the LADOT Citywide Investigations Unit at (213) 928-9625 at the following points in time, and for the following purposes:
 A. Ten (10) working days in advance of markout.
 B. Upon completion of markout (including any markout corrections) for inspection and approval. Upon approval of markout, the contractor shall install the thermoplastic striping within five (5) working days.
 C. Upon completion of thermoplastic striping (including any thermoplastic striping corrections) for inspection and final striping approval.
3. During all phases of construction, temporary raised overlay pavement markers shall be maintained adjacent to the temporary centerline, markout centerline, or scar of a sandblasted centerline, as applicable, as per LADOT Standard Plan No. S-453.0.
4. The field conditions shown as existing on this plan may change between the plan approval date and the implementation date. The B-Permittee may be required to install or remove striping, pavement markings, signs or other traffic control devices beyond those indicated on this plan, in order to facilitate these changes in field conditions and/or to be in compliance with LADOT standards and specifications. If this plan has not been installed within two (2) years of the accepted date, it shall be resubmitted to LADOT for reapproval prior to proceeding to construction.
5. Removal and reinstallation of parking meters: The contractor shall contact the LADOT Parking Meter Administrator at (213) 473-8270 five (5) working days in advance of construction affecting parking meters. LADOT will coordinate the removal of parking meters and signs as needed and, upon completion of the project, the reinstallation of meters, signs, and/or paint as needed. Removal and reinstallation costs will be deducted from the contractors deposit. Failure to notify LADOT will make the contractor liable for the cost of any missing or damaged meters, signs, etc., that the department records indicate were present.
[6] Remove conflicting striping. Install continental crosswalks per LADOT Std. Dwg. No. S-481.1.
[7] Contractor shall contact City-wide Investigation Office, at (213) 928-9625 to coordinate removal of stop sign (R1-1) and pavement markings at time of signal activation.
8. Contractor shall inspect and ensure that the final roadway surface is in good condition prior to bike lane installation.

Legend:
1. Existing striping and markings to remain. Existing striping and markings to be removed. Proposed striping and markings.
2. Existing sign and post. Existing sign and post to be removed or relocated. Proposed sign and post.
3. Signalized intersection (circled S).
4. Existing red curb markings (R/C) to remain. Existing red curb markings to be removed. Proposed red curb markings.

Notes:
1. Length of design: 1045 ft +/-.
2. Install pavement (PVMT.) markings as shown.
3. Paint removal required.
4. Continental crosswalk per LADOT Std. Dwg. No. S-481.1.

Sign panel codes: R3-4, R3-2, R9-3, R9-3bP(RT), R9-3bP(LT), R61-7(CA), R3-7(RT), SW44(LT)(CA), ASSEMBLY A (SCHOOL), R61-19(CA).

Abbreviations as drawn: red curb (R/C), white (W.), tow-away no stopping any time (T.A.N.S.A.T.), no parking any time (N.P.A.T.), parking meter zone (PMZ), typical (TYP.), property line (PL), corner radius (CR). The abbreviations A.G.Z. and T.A.N.S. appear in parking text and are not expanded on the sheet.
Certification statement: Pursuant to the California Business and Professions Code, this plan is prepared by and under the responsible charge of work of, the named consulting firm and California Registered Engineers shown below.
Title block note: If this plan has not been implemented within two (2) years of the acceptance date, it must be resubmitted to LADOT for review and acceptance.
title: Sample Geometric Plan: Signing and Striping Plan Sheet
summary: Sample LADOT B-Permit signing and striping plan for "A" Avenue between "B" Street and "C" Street at 1 inch = 40 feet. The middle shows low brick and white buildings, including a white building with two domes and a mid-rise building with a green top. The lower half looks down a multilane street with lane lines, a crosswalk marked in red with three pedestrians in it, a yellow school bus, a brown delivery truck, a van and a white sedan. A wide sidewalk with a line of short bollards or posts runs along the left side of the street, shaded by trees and palms. On the right is a fabric-roofed shelter, traffic signals with yellow-green pedestrian crossing signs on the mast arms, a green guide sign, and white pavement text partly visible near the bottom. A flagpole with an American flag stands at the left foreground. No captions or credits are shown.

It shows a tree-lined sidewalk with a row of bollards, a red-painted crosswalk with pedestrians, a school bus and delivery truck, and brick and white institutional buildings. The page has no text.

In the upper right, a large square white sign with a black border shows a red YIELD triangle at the top, the word HERE at the left, a black curved arrow pointing down and to the left, the word TO and a black walking pedestrian symbol. It is mounted on a perforated galvanized post. Below and to the right, a fluorescent yellow-green diamond pedestrian crossing sign and a smaller yellow-green plaque with a diagonal arrow pointing down and to the left hang on an ornate decorative lamp post. A blue street name sign (partly visible, beginning 27), a yellow AHEAD plaque and a small bicycle sign appear further down the same post. The lower half shows a street with a pedestrian crossing in a white high-visibility crosswalk of wide bars, a blue sedan, a dark sedan and a yellow school bus in the lane beyond, with a maroon-painted curb at the right and a sidewalk and decorative lamp post at the lower right. No captions or credits are shown.
notes: Lettering visible in the photograph: YIELD (inside the red triangle), HERE, TO, and the SCHOOL BUS lettering on the bus. No captions or credits.

description: Photograph: a full-bleed portrait photo of a light rail station. At the top right is a dark station canopy with translucent yellow roof panels and a black directional sign with a white arrow pointing down and to the left and the words Los Angeles. Below it hang two electronic arrival displays in orange text, one reading :25pm 2:37pm and another partly visible, and a partial sign reading Flo... St. At the left, the front of a white and gold-striped light rail car faces the camera. Its destination display reads BLUE LINE in orange, a windshield display reads 112, the car numbers 136 and 136B are visible, and a circular M roundel is centered below the windshield. Rails run in the foreground. At the right, a platform edge with a tan tactile warning surface of small domes lies next to a yellow edge line with the text STAY BEHIND YELLOW LINE printed along it. Several passengers stand on the gray tiled platform, one with a stroller, one in a purple varsity jacket and one in a blue cap. A blue pole stands at the far left. Credit text in italic at the lower left of the photograph reads PHOTO: LADOTBIKEBLOG, FLICKR.
notes: Text in the photograph: BLUE LINE, 112, 136, 136B, Los Angeles, 2:37pm, STAY BEHIND YELLOW LINE, Exit Trade Tech (partly visible). Credit: PHOTO: LADOTBIKEBLOG, FLICKR.
title: Photograph: Light Rail Train at a Station Platform

A photo credit to LADOT Bike Blog on Flickr appears at the lower left.

Along the right side, people stand by a curb with pink curb paint, pink hand-lettered signs and parking meters. A low concrete balustrade lines the park edge at the left. description:
Plan view: a straight arterial runs left to right with a double yellow centerline, dashed lane lines and a left-turn pocket on the left drawn with a curved bay taper and a left-turn arrow, and a second, hatched pocket taper in the middle. A side street intersects the arterial at the upper left, with a stop sign R1-1 called out on its corner post. A fire station sits on the north side, labeled Fire Station, with its driveway drawn as a crossed box on the north side of the roadway. Two beacon installations flank the driveway. On the north side, a pole east of the driveway at 5 ft to 20 ft from the driveway edge carries a mast arm marked 20 ft min. M.A. with two flashing beacons and is keyed Detail A, with a cable line running to an activation switch located inside the fire station. On the south side, a second pole and mast arm marked 20 ft min. M.A. and keyed Detail A is located 0 ft to 20 ft from the driveway centerline (dimension 0'~20'). Pull boxes and a conduit run are drawn along the south curb. A leader at the far left reads: Interconnect cable to controller at adjacent signal if Condition C is satisfied or within 300 feet (see Note 3). A note below the plan reads: Final street lighting may not include the depicted mast arm lighting shown.
Detail A: a black-on-yellow diamond fire truck sign W11-8 (36 in.) is centered between two square signal housings, each holding a circled Y for a 12 in. yellow beacon. Wires from each beacon curve to the sign.
Authorization: text list as given in the notes. Operation: text list as given in the notes.
Title block: S-60.0, sheet 1/1, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, drawn by MT 9-30-15, T.E. JV 9-30-15, Sr. T.E. MA 10-1-15, Pr. T.E. VJ 10-2-15, approved by Seleta Reynolds, General Manager, 11-20-15.
notes:
Plan notes:
- To activation switch located inside Fire Station.
- Dimensions: 0 ft to 20 ft and 5 ft to 20 ft (as drawn 0'~20' and 5'~20').
- 20 ft minimum (min.) mast arm (M.A.) at each beacon pole (Detail A).
- Interconnect cable to controller at adjacent signal if Condition C is satisfied or within 300 feet (see Note 3).
- Final street lighting may not include the depicted mast arm lighting shown.
- Detail A: sign W11-8 (36 in.) with two 12 in. yellow beacons (circled Y). Stop sign R1-1 at the side street corner.

Authorization
Fire Station Warning Beacons shown on this plan are authorized when:
1. There are existing warning beacons that flash all-day or during non-emergency periods and it is desired to retain some form of warning beacons, or
2. There are no existing warning beacons, the Fire Station Captain requests or concurs with the installation of Fire Station Warning Beacons, and an engineering study using LADOT guidelines documents Condition A, B, C or D below:
 A. An accident pattern involving emergency vehicles at or near the fire station driveway.
 B. The cross traffic visibility between the emergency vehicle driver and arterial street motorists is less than an acceptable gap.
 C. The queue extending from a nearby signal recurrently blocks the fire station driveway and "KEEP CLEAR" pavement markings have not been effective.
 D. There is an excess of 30 seconds of delay for exiting emergency vehicles.

Operation
1. The beacons are dark in the absence of a manual emergency response activation.
2. Upon an emergency response, a station officer manually activates a switch to commence flashing of the yellow beacons. The beacons immediately flash alternately in push/pull fashion. The duration of emergency flashing operation generally is 45 seconds. The warning signs and flashing beacons complement Section 21806 of the California Vehicle Code, regarding driver and pedestrian responsibilities near authorized emergency vehicles. They serve to alert motorists when an emergency is in effect and where emergency vehicles will be entering the street.
3. If Condition C is satisfied or if there is an adjacent traffic signal within 300 feet, then it should operate under preemption operation. This preemption operation will hold vehicles from approaching the fire station in one direction, allow queued vehicles to clear the driveway in the opposite direction and enable emergency vehicles to clear the intersection. The operation is as follows: The phase receiving the green goes to normal pedestrian and yellow clearances followed by 3 seconds of all-red for all approaches with an opposing, permissive left-turn, in order to preclude a left-turn trap situation. Then the approach to the adjacent signalized intersection, which is on the departure from the Fire Station, goes to green and stays in green. All other vehicle approaches stay in red and pedestrian indications provide a solid Upraised Hand (Don't Walk) display.
4. At the end of emergency preemption, normal signal operation resumes from the current position. Flashing yellow beacons are extinguished.
title: Fire Station Warning Beacons (Standard Drawing S-60.0)
summary: LADOT standard drawing S-60.0 for yellow warning beacons at fire station driveways. The plan shows beacon mast arm locations, the interconnect to an adjacent signal and an activation switch inside the station, with Detail A showing the W11-8 sign and two 12 inch yellow beacons. The text gives when beacons are authorized (Conditions A to D) and how they operate, including a 45 second flash and signal preemption when Condition C applies or a signal is within 300 feet.

description:
Intro text: For multiple lane approaches, loop detectors should be centered in lanes. For curb lane, follow the guidelines for single lane approach.
Plan views: two mirror-image diagrams of a signalized intersection (circled S) with crosswalks on all legs show a four-lane approach. The left diagram is the approach on the left side of the intersection and the right diagram is the approach on the right side. Each shows four lanes with a left-turn lane (curved arrow) next to the center line, and a pair of loops in each lane (front loop nearest the limit line drawn with a diagonal slash as a bicycle detector, rear loop open). Leads from all loops fan to a single pull box or stub-out at the curb. The callout Centered in lane points to the loops in the three lanes nearest the center line. The callout See guidelines on single lane approaches points to the curb lane loops. Dimensions A, B, C and D are stacked from the curb face to the loops of the successive lanes, with A for the curb lane. The limit line is dimensioned 5 ft from the crosswalk on the left diagram, and an 8 ft dimension on the right diagram gives the separation between front and rear loops. A caption reads Multiple Lane Approaches.
Notes block: six numbered notes as listed.
Title block: Limit Line Inductive Loop Detector Placement, sheet 2/2, drawing S-70.0, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation.
notes:
Multiple lane approaches: For multiple lane approaches, loop detectors should be centered in lanes. For curb lane, follow the guidelines for single lane approach. See guidelines on single lane approaches (callout at the curb lane loops). Loops are centered in lanes (callout).

Notes:
1. This Standard Drawing applies to new installations and re-installations due to maintenance. Loop detectors should be re-installed at existing locations where the loop detectors extend 4 ft or more into marked crosswalks and limit lines.
2. All loops are 6 ft diameter with 8 ft separation between front and rear loops.
3. A, B, C, D dimensions shall be shown on plans.
4. The loop detectors adjacent to the limit line shall be bicycle detectors.
5. See Standard Drawing Nos. S-70.1A and S-70.1D for installation details.
6. Types and locations of conduits, pullboxes and stub-outs to be installed per plan.

description:
Left panel, Ped-Actuated Pedestrian Crossing (pushbutton activates accessible pedestrian signals and the WALK interval): a small plan sketch of a crosswalk with two corners, each corner showing a curved curb with a pedestrian head symbol and an APS pushbutton, labeled phi 2 APS on both sides and 2p heads. Beside it is an enlarged elevation of the APS unit. Its display panel has four stacked indications: START CROSSING with a walking person symbol and Watch For Vehicles, DON'T START with a flashing orange hand, Finish Crossing If Started and a TIMER display with TIME REMAINING To Finish Crossing, DON'T CROSS with a steady orange hand, and a PUSH BUTTON TO CROSS panel with an arrow. Below is the round pushbutton with a raised arrow and a PATENT number plate. A leader at the base reads Wires to controller pedestrian pushbutton (PPB) input.
Right panel, Pre-Timed & Rest-in-Walk Pedestrian Crossing (pushbutton activates accessible pedestrian signals only. WALK interval is on recall): the same crosswalk sketch (labeled APS) and the same APS unit, but without the PUSH BUTTON TO CROSS panel. The leader at the base reads No wires connected to controller pedestrian pushbutton (PPB) input.
Notes block: eight numbered notes as listed.
Title block: Accessible Pedestrian Signal (APS), sheet 1/2, drawing S-73.2, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, drawn by MT 6-27-16, T.E. JV 7-7-16, Sr. T.E. MA 8-3-16, Pr. T.E. VJ 8-9-16, approved by Seleta J. Reynolds, General Manager, 8-9-16.
notes:
Display and unit labels: START CROSSING, Watch For Vehicles. DON'T START, Finish Crossing If Started (flashing), TIME REMAINING To Finish Crossing (timer). DON'T CROSS (steady). PUSH BUTTON TO CROSS (ped-actuated unit only). Wires to controller pedestrian pushbutton (PPB) input (ped-actuated). No wires connected to controller pedestrian pushbutton (PPB) input (pre-timed and rest-in-walk).

Notes:
1. APS shall be used for situations where new pedestrian pushbuttons are being installed or where they are being replaced, due to maintenance.
2. Audio specifications:
 WALK interval: Rapid "Tick" tone is activated with a duration of 0.15 seconds and repeats at 0.25-second intervals for a maximum of 7 seconds. Then, APS returns to locator tone for the remainder of the WALK interval.
 FLASHING DON'T WALK interval and SOLID DON'T WALK interval: Locator tone shall have a duration of 0.15 seconds and repeat at 1-second intervals.
3. Vibrotactile specifications:
 Pushbutton vibrates only during the first 7 seconds of the WALK interval.
 Tactile arrows shall be aligned parallel to the direction of travel on the associated crosswalk.
 WALK tones and vibrotactile require actuation, even at pre-timed crossings.
4. See California MUTCD 2014, Figures 4E-3 and 4E-4 for pushbutton locations.
5. Countdown pedestrian heads shall be installed at all accessible pedestrian signal locations.
6. See sheet 2/2 for accessible pedestrian signal field wiring for ped-actuated pedestrian crossing.
7. Low Voltage "Grey Cable" on sheet 2/2 refers to manufacturer supplied cable that is included with the APS unit.
8. 4cc on sheet 2/2 as per LADOT Spec. 92-097-01.
title: Accessible Pedestrian Signal (APS), Sheet 1 of 2 (Standard Drawing S-73.2)
summary: LADOT standard drawing S-73.2 sheet 1 of 2 comparing two accessible pedestrian signal (APS) arrangements. A ped-actuated crossing has the pushbutton activating the APS and the WALK interval, while a pre-timed or rest-in-walk crossing has the pushbutton activate the APS only with WALK on recall. The sheet gives the audio and vibrotactile specifications and says APS is used wherever new pushbuttons are installed or replaced for maintenance.

description:
Arrangement 1, APS pushbutton and associated pedestrian head on same pole for ped-actuated pedestrian crossing: a corner plan key shows one pole, circled 1, with a 4p pedestrian head and a phase 4 APS pushbutton at the curb return, with a crosswalk beside it. The wiring schematic for pole 1 shows the pole with a terminal block (Y, BLK, R, BRN against D/W, W, D/W, W, C), a PED HEAD (4p) box with an APS control unit terminal strip (A/C, BRN, R, G, W, C, D/W with + and - low voltage, W D/W) and an LED PED module terminal strip (W, C, D/W). Low voltage gray cable runs from the pushbutton (phase 4 APS button) to the control unit. 3 CC (or 2 #14) PPB wires and 5 CC for ped phase run from the pole base to a PULL BOX.
Arrangement 2, APS pushbutton and associated pedestrian head not on same pole: the plan key shows poles 1 and 2 at the corner. Pole 1 carries a 2p head and the phase 4 APS button, and pole 2 at the crosswalk end carries a 4p head and the phase 2 APS button. The schematics show pole 1 with a PED HEAD (2p) and pole 2 with a PED HEAD (4p), each with APS control unit, terminal block and low voltage gray cable, a phase APS button near the base, 3 CC (or 2 #14) PPB wires, 5 CC for ped phase and two connected PULL BOX symbols with a SPARES (5 CC if no spares) run between them.
Arrangement 3, APS pushbutton on Type 7 post and associated pedestrian head not on same pole: the plan key shows a Type 7 post (circled 1) at the corner with the phase 4 APS button, pole 2 with a 2p head and pole 3 with a 4p head and the phase 2 APS button. The schematics show the Type 7 post with a 4 CC cable run, 3 CC (or 2 #14) PPB wires to a pull box, pole 2 with a PED HEAD (2p) and 4 CC, and pole 3 with a PED HEAD (4p), 5 CC for ped phase and low voltage gray cable, connected through pull boxes with SPARES (5 CC if no spares).
Title block: Accessible Pedestrian Signal (APS), sheet 2/2, drawing S-73.2, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation.
notes:
Labels, arrangement 1 (pushbutton and pedestrian head on same pole): PED HEAD (4p), APS control unit, low voltage, LED ped module, low voltage "gray cable", phase 4 APS button (phi 4 APS BUTTON), 3 CC (or 2 #14) PPB wires, 5 CC for ped phase, pull box, A/C.
Labels, arrangement 2 (not on same pole): PED HEAD (2p) and PED HEAD (4p), APS control unit, low voltage "gray cable", phi 4 APS button and phi 2 APS button, 3 CC (or 2 #14) PPB wires, 5 CC for ped phase, pull box, spares (5 CC if no spares).
Labels, arrangement 3 (Type 7 post): PED HEAD (2p) and PED HEAD (4p), APS control unit, Type 7 post, phi 4 APS button and phi 2 APS button, low voltage "gray cable", 4 CC, 5 CC for ped phase, 3 CC (or 2 #14) PPB wires, pull box, spares (5 CC if no spares).
Terminal and wire color codes as drawn: BLK (black), BRN (brown), R (red), Y (yellow), W (white), G (green), C (common), D/W (don't walk).
Cable abbreviation: conductor cable (CC). Notes 6 to 8 on sheet 1/2 apply to this sheet.
title: Accessible Pedestrian Signal (APS), Field Wiring, Sheet 2 of 2 (Standard Drawing S-73.2)
summary: LADOT standard drawing S-73.2 sheet 2 of 2 giving field wiring diagrams for ped-actuated crossings with accessible pedestrian signals. Three arrangements are shown: the APS pushbutton and pedestrian head on the same pole, on different poles, and with the pushbutton on a Type 7 post. Each includes a corner plan key, pole and pull box wiring schematics and cable counts such as 3 CC (or 2 #14) PPB wires, 4 CC and 5 CC for ped phase.

description:
Right Jog: a plan view of a signalized (circled S) intersection where the minor street enters from the bottom at the left side and continues out the top at the right side, so the two legs are offset across the arterial. Crosswalks are drawn on the arterial approaches and on the minor street legs. Four vehicles are drawn inside the intersection with dashed path lines. One path curves from the lower minor street leg up and to the right toward the upper leg, one vehicle heads toward the right through the intersection, and the others run in the arterial. Two pedestrians are shown in the east crosswalk. Four bullet points sit to the right of the diagram, listed in the notes.
Left Jog: a similar plan view where the minor street enters from the bottom at the right side and exits at the top at the left side. Two vehicles are drawn with dashed path lines crossing diagonally through the intersection, and two pedestrians are drawn in the east crosswalk. Five bullet points sit to the right of the diagram, listed in the notes.
Caption and instruction: Operational Challenges for the Minor Street Approaches to Signalized Jogged Intersections. To select the most appropriate design for minimizing the above challenges see Sheet 2.
Title block: Operation and Design of Signalized Jogged Intersections, sheet 1/12, drawing S-100.0, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, drawn by EC 6-10-10, approved June 24, 2010, Rita L. Robinson, General Manager (signed for).
notes:
Right Jog:
- Pedestrians might not be seen early-on by right-turning motorists.
- Opposing vehicles might not be seen early-on.
- Opposing arterial left turns might interlock.

Left Jog:
- Pedestrians might not be seen early-on by left-turning motorists.
- Opposing vehicles might not be seen early-on.
- Opposing left turns interlock.
- Difficult to determine if motorist is making a left turn or jogged through move.
- So-called opposing moves momentarily can be positioned at approximately right angles to each other.

Operational Challenges for the Minor Street Approaches to Signalized Jogged Intersections. To select the most appropriate design for minimizing the above challenges see Sheet 2.
title: Operational Challenges for the Minor Street Approaches to Signalized Jogged Intersections (Standard Drawing S-100.0, Sheet 1 of 12)
summary: LADOT standard drawing S-100.0 sheet 1 of 12 for the operation and design of signalized jogged intersections. It illustrates, for a right jog and a left jog, the operational challenges on the minor street approaches, such as pedestrians and opposing vehicles not being seen early and opposing left turns interlocking. The design selection procedure itself is on Sheet 2.
